column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|02-18|1931|Τόνι Μόρρισον|Toni Morrison|Toni Morrison was an American writer. She wrote novels about the experience of African Americans, such as "Beloved" and "The Bluest Eye". In 1993 she became the first Black woman to be honoured with the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-18|1933|Γιόκο Όνο|Yoko Ono|Yoko Ono was born in Tokyo and is an artist and musician. She took part in the Fluxus movement and created performance and conceptual art. She was married to John Lennon and worked with him for peace.

bio|02-18|1954|Τζον Τραβόλτα|John Travolta|John Travolta is an American actor. He became famous with "Saturday Night Fever" and "Grease" and returned to fame with Tarantino's "Pulp Fiction", for which he was nominated for an Oscar.

bio|02-18|1967|Ρόμπερτ Οπενχάιμερ|Robert Oppenheimer|Robert Oppenheimer was an American physicist. He led the Los Alamos laboratory in the Manhattan Project and is regarded as the "father of the atomic bomb". After the war his loyalty was questioned and his access to classified information was withdrawn.

bio|02-19|1473|Νικόλαος Κοπέρνικος|Nicolaus Copernicus|Nicolaus Copernicus was a Polish astronomer. In his work "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres" in 1543 he argued that the Earth and the other planets move around the Sun, changing the picture of the universe.

bio|02-19|1859|Σβάντε Αρρένιους|Svante Arrhenius|Svante Arrhenius was a Swedish chemist. He formulated the Arrhenius equation for the rate of chemical reactions and wrote about the effect of carbon dioxide on the temperature of the Earth. In 1903 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|02-19|1896|Αντρέ Μπρετόν|Andre Breton|Andre Breton was a French poet and theorist, and the founder of surrealism. In 1924 he published the "Manifesto of Surrealism" and wrote "Nadja". He influenced painters and writers.

bio|02-19|1940|Σαπαρμουράτ Νιγιαζόφ|Saparmurat Niyazov|Saparmurat Niyazov was the first president of Turkmenistan after independence. He ruled from 1991 to 2006 in an authoritarian way and created a cult of his personality, with the title "Turkmenbashi".

bio|02-19|1951|Αντρέ Ζιντ|Andre Gide|Andre Gide was a French writer. He wrote "The Counterfeiters" and "The Immoralist". He was one of the founders of the journal "Nouvelle Revue Francaise", and in 1947 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-19|1952|Κνουτ Χάμσουν|Knut Hamsun|Knut Hamsun was a Norwegian writer. He wrote the novel "Hunger" and "Growth of the Soil", for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1920. His support for the Nazis during the Second World War tarnished his reputation.

bio|02-19|1953|Κριστίνα Φερνάντες ντε Κίρχνερ|Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner|Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner is an Argentine politician. She was president of Argentina from 2007 to 2015, succeeding her husband Nestor Kirchner, and vice president from 2019 to 2023.

bio|02-19|1997|Τενγκ Σιαοπίνγκ|Deng Xiaoping|Deng Xiaoping was the leader of China from 1978 to the 1990s. He launched economic reforms and opened the country to the market, but kept the rule of the Communist Party. He also ordered the crackdown in Tiananmen Square in 1989.

bio|02-19|2016|Ουμπέρτο Έκο|Umberto Eco|Umberto Eco died in Milan in 2016. He was an Italian semiotician and the author of the novel "The Name of the Rose", with a great influence on the philosophy of language and on literary theory.

bio|02-20|1054|Γιαροσλάβ Α΄ ο Σοφός|Yaroslav the Wise|Yaroslav the Wise was grand prince of Kiev from 1019 to 1054. He codified the law of Kievan Rus, known as the "Russkaya Pravda", built the Cathedral of Saint Sophia in Kiev and strengthened ties with Europe.

bio|02-20|1778|Λάουρα Μπάσσι|Laura Bassi|Laura Bassi was an Italian physicist. In 1732 she became the first woman to hold a university chair in physics in Europe, at Bologna. She spread the ideas of Newton in Italy.

bio|02-20|1790|Ιωσήφ Β΄ των Αψβούργων|Joseph II|Joseph II was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and ruler of the Habsburg lands. He was a representative of "enlightened despotism" and carried out reforms, such as the abolition of serfdom and religious tolerance.

bio|02-20|1844|Λούντβιχ Μπόλτσμαν|Ludwig Boltzmann|Ludwig Boltzmann was an Austrian physicist. He developed statistical mechanics and linked entropy with probability. His equation for entropy is inscribed on his tomb in Vienna.

bio|02-20|1927|Σίντνεϊ Πουατιέ|Sidney Poitier|Sidney Poitier was an American actor and director, born in Miami. In 1964 he became the first African American to win the Oscar for Best Actor, for "Lilies of the Field".

bio|02-20|1951|Γκόρντον Μπράουν|Gordon Brown|Gordon Brown is a Scottish Labour politician. He was chancellor of the Exchequer of Britain from 1997 to 2007 and prime minister from 2007 to 2010, during the global financial crisis.

bio|02-20|1967|Κερτ Κομπέιν|Kurt Cobain|Kurt Cobain was an American musician, singer and guitarist of Nirvana. The band became famous with the album "Nevermind" in 1991. He took his own life in 1994, at the age of 27.

bio|02-20|1972|Μαρία Γκέπερτ-Μάγιερ|Maria Goeppert-Mayer|Maria Goeppert-Mayer was born in Germany and lived in the United States. She was a physicist and developed the shell model of the nucleus. In 1963 she became the second woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-20|1988|Ριάννα|Rihanna|Rihanna was born in Barbados and is a singer and businesswoman. She became famous with songs such as "Umbrella" and "Diamonds". She founded the cosmetics company Fenty Beauty.

bio|02-21|1677|Μπαρούχ Σπινόζα|Baruch Spinoza|Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher of Jewish descent. His main work, "Ethics", argues that God and nature are identical. He was excommunicated by the Jewish community of Amsterdam and earned his living by making lenses.

bio|02-21|1801|Τζον Χένρι Νιούμαν|John Henry Newman|John Henry Newman was an English theologian. He was a clergyman of the Church of England and converted to Catholicism in 1845. He became a cardinal and was declared a saint by the Catholic Church in 2019.

bio|02-21|1907|Ουίσταν Ώντεν|W. H. Auden|W. H. Auden was born in England and lived in the United States. He was a poet of the twentieth century and wrote poems such as "In Memory of W. B. Yeats" and "The Shield of Achilles". "Funeral Blues" became famous through the film "Four Weddings and a Funeral".

bio|02-21|1924|Ρόμπερτ Μουγκάμπε|Robert Mugabe|Robert Mugabe was the leader of Zimbabwe after its independence in 1980. He was prime minister and then president until 2017. His rule was authoritarian and the economy collapsed. He was overthrown by the army.

bio|02-21|1926|Χάικε Κάμερλιν|Heike Kamerlingh Onnes|Heike Kamerlingh Onnes was a Dutch physicist. In 1911 he discovered superconductivity in mercury, and in 1913 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his study of the behaviour of matter at very low temperatures.

bio|02-21|1937|Χάραλντ Ε΄|Harald V|Harald V has been king of Norway since 1991, when his father Olav V died. He was an Olympic sailor. He married Sonja Haraldsen, despite initial objections, because she was not from a royal family.

bio|02-21|1965|Μάλκολμ Χ|Malcolm X|Malcolm X was an African American activist and speaker. He was a spokesman for the Nation of Islam and after the 1960s he left the organisation. He was assassinated in New York in 1965.

bio|02-21|1984|Μιχαήλ Σόλοχοφ|Mikhail Sholokhov|Mikhail Sholokhov was a Russian writer. He wrote the epic novel "And Quiet Flows the Don" about the Don Cossacks during the time of war and revolution. In 1965 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|02-21|1989|Κόρμπιν Μπλου|Corbin Bleu|Corbin Bleu is an American actor and singer. He became known for the role of Chad in the film "High School Musical" and in Disney Channel series.

bio|02-22|1512|Αμέριγκο Βεσπούτσι|Amerigo Vespucci|Amerigo Vespucci was an Italian explorer and cartographer from Florence. He travelled to the New World and argued that it was a new continent. America took its name from his first name.

bio|02-22|1732|Τζορτζ Ουάσινγκτον|George Washington|George Washington was the leader of the Continental Army in the American War of Independence and the first president of the United States, from 1789 to 1797. He refused to serve a third term and established the peaceful transfer of power.

bio|02-22|1788|Άρθουρ Σοπενχάουερ|Arthur Schopenhauer|Arthur Schopenhauer was a German philosopher. His main work, "The World as Will and Representation", argues that the will is the basis of reality. He had a pessimistic view of life and influenced Nietzsche and Wagner.

bio|02-22|1857|Χάινριχ Χερτζ|Heinrich Hertz|Heinrich Hertz was a German physicist. He demonstrated experimentally the existence of electromagnetic waves. The unit of frequency, the hertz, is named after him. He died young, in 1894.

bio|02-22|1857|Ρόμπερτ Μπέηντεν-Πάουελ|Robert Baden-Powell|Robert Baden-Powell was a British soldier and the founder of the Scout movement. He became known for the defence of Mafeking in the Boer War, and in 1907 he organised the first scout camp.

bio|02-22|1875|Ζαν-Μπατίστ Καμίλ Κορό|Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot|Camille Corot was a French landscape painter. He painted rural scenes in soft colours and was a forerunner of Impressionism. He died in Paris in 1875.

bio|02-22|1913|Φερντινάντ ντε Σωσσύρ|Ferdinand de Saussure|Ferdinand de Saussure was a Swiss linguist. His work "Course in General Linguistics", published by his students, founded structural linguistics and semiology. It influenced the social sciences.

bio|02-22|1975|Ντρου Μπάριμορ|Drew Barrymore|Drew Barrymore is an American actress and producer. She became known as a child in the film "E.T." and later appeared in films such as "The Wedding Singer" and "Charlie's Angels".

bio|02-22|1987|Άντι Γουόρχολ|Andy Warhol|Andy Warhol was an American artist and a leading figure of pop art. He became known for his series of Campbell's soup cans and for portraits of Marilyn Monroe. He founded "The Factory" studio in New York.

bio|02-23|1685|Γκέοργκ Φρήντριχ Χέντελ|George Frideric Handel|George Frideric Handel was born in Germany and lived most of his years in England. He was a Baroque composer and wrote the oratorio "Messiah", with the "Hallelujah" chorus, and the works "Water Music".

bio|02-23|1821|Τζον Κητς|John Keats|John Keats was an English poet of the Romantic movement. He wrote odes such as "Ode to a Nightingale" and "Ode on a Grecian Urn". He died of tuberculosis in Rome in 1821, at the age of twenty-six.

bio|02-23|1848|Τζον Κουίνσι Άνταμς|John Quincy Adams|John Quincy Adams was the 6th president of the United States, from 1825 to 1829. He was the son of the second president John Adams and had served as secretary of state. After his presidency he served as a member of Congress and opposed slavery.

bio|02-23|1855|Καρλ Φρίντριχ Γκάους|Carl Friedrich Gauss|Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician, astronomer and physicist. He is regarded as one of the greatest mathematicians of all time. He contributed to number theory, geometry and statistics with the normal distribution.

bio|02-23|1879|Καζιμίρ Μαλέβιτς|Kazimir Malevich|Kazimir Malevich was a Russian painter. He was the founder of Suprematism, a movement of abstract art, and became known for the painting "Black Square" of 1915.

bio|02-23|1883|Καρλ Γιάσπερς|Karl Jaspers|Karl Jaspers was a German psychiatrist and philosopher. He became one of the main representatives of existentialist philosophy and wrote "General Psychopathology". He taught at Heidelberg and Basel.

bio|02-23|1942|Στέφαν Τσβάιχ|Stefan Zweig|Stefan Zweig was an Austrian writer. He wrote biographies, short stories and "The World of Yesterday". Because of his Jewish origin he left Europe, and in 1942 he took his own life in Brazil, together with his wife.

bio|02-23|1954|Βίκτορ Γιούστσενκο|Viktor Yushchenko|Viktor Yushchenko is a Ukrainian politician. He was president of Ukraine from 2005 to 2010, after the Orange Revolution. In 2004 he was poisoned with dioxin and survived.
bio|02-23|1983|Έμιλι Μπλαντ|Emily Blunt|Emily Blunt is an English actress. She became known for her role in "The Devil Wears Prada" and appeared in films such as "Edge of Tomorrow" and "Oppenheimer".

bio|02-24|1304|Ιμπν Μπατούτα|Ibn Battuta|Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan explorer. He travelled for decades across much of the Muslim world and beyond, from Africa to China. The account of his journeys, the "Rihla", is an important source.

bio|02-24|1500|Κάρολος Κουίντος|Charles V|Charles V was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and king of Spain. His empire extended across Europe and into the New World. He faced the Reformation and the Ottomans, and he abdicated in 1556.

bio|02-24|1810|Χένρι Κάβεντις|Henry Cavendish|Henry Cavendish was a British physicist and chemist. He discovered hydrogen and measured the density of the Earth with the Cavendish experiment. He was extremely introverted and published little.

bio|02-24|1815|Ρόμπερτ Φούλτον|Robert Fulton|Robert Fulton was an American engineer and inventor. In 1807 he made commercial use of the steamboat "Clermont" on the Hudson River and developed steam navigation. He also designed a submarine.

bio|02-24|1955|Στιβ Τζομπς|Steve Jobs|Steve Jobs was an American businessman. In 1976 he founded Apple with Steve Wozniak and later led Pixar. He presented the iPod, the iPhone and the iPad. He died of cancer in 2011.

bio|02-24|1956|Τζούντιθ Μπάτλερ|Judith Butler|Judith Butler is an American philosopher and gender theorist. Her book "Gender Trouble" of 1990 influenced gender studies and queer theory. She teaches at Berkeley.

bio|02-24|1977|Φλόιντ Μεϊγουέδερ Τζ.|Floyd Mayweather Jr.|Floyd Mayweather Jr. is a former American boxer. He won world titles in five weight classes and retired undefeated, with 50 wins in 50 fights.

bio|02-24|2001|Κλοντ Σάνον|Claude Shannon|Claude Shannon was an American mathematician and engineer. In 1948 he published "A Mathematical Theory of Communication", which founded information theory and influenced digital computers.

bio|02-24|2003|Αλμπέρτο Σόρντι|Alberto Sordi|Alberto Sordi was an Italian actor and director. He appeared in many Italian comedies, such as "The Marquis of Grillo", and was one of Italy's leading comedians.

bio|02-25|1707|Κάρλο Γκολντόνι|Carlo Goldoni|Carlo Goldoni was born in Venice. He was a playwright and reformed the Italian theatre, replacing the commedia dell'arte with written plays and realistic characters, such as "La Locandiera".

bio|02-25|1778|Χοσέ ντε Σαν Μαρτίν|Jose de San Martin|Jose de San Martin was an Argentine general. He led the struggle for the independence of Argentina, Chile and Peru from Spain, and is regarded as a national hero of Argentina.

bio|02-25|1841|Πιερ-Ωγκύστ Ρενουάρ|Pierre-Auguste Renoir|Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French painter and one of the founders of Impressionism. He became known for his bright works, such as "Luncheon of the Boating Party" and "Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette".

bio|02-25|1866|Μπενεντέτο Κρότσε|Benedetto Croce|Benedetto Croce was an Italian philosopher, historian and politician. He was a liberal and opposed fascism. He wrote on aesthetics and history and was one of the most important Italian intellectuals.

bio|02-25|1873|Ενρίκο Καρούζο|Enrico Caruso|Enrico Caruso was an Italian tenor from Naples. He was one of the first artists to sell millions of records. He was known for his powerful and rich voice and sang at the Metropolitan Opera.

bio|02-25|1970|Μαρκ Ρόθκο|Mark Rothko|Mark Rothko was born in Latvia and lived in the United States. He was a painter of abstract expressionism and became known for paintings with large fields of colour. He took his own life in 1970.

bio|02-25|1983|Τενεσί Ουίλιαμς|Tennessee Williams|Tennessee Williams was an American playwright. He wrote the plays "The Glass Menagerie", "A Streetcar Named Desire" and "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof", and he won the Pulitzer Prize.

bio|02-25|1999|Γκλεν Θ. Σίμποργκ|Glenn T. Seaborg|Glenn T. Seaborg was an American chemist. He contributed to the discovery of ten chemical elements with higher atomic numbers than uranium. In 1951 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. The element seaborgium is named after him.

bio|02-25|2014|Πάκο ντε Λουθία|Paco de Lucia|Paco de Lucia was a Spanish flamenco guitarist. He became famous internationally, especially for his performance of "Entre dos aguas". He collaborated with jazz and classical musicians.

bio|02-26|1154|Ρογήρος Β΄|Roger II|Roger II was king of Sicily from 1130 to 1154. He founded the Norman kingdom of Sicily and was known for his tolerance of different peoples and cultures. He encouraged the development of the arts and sciences in Palermo.
bio|02-26|1770|Τζουζέπε Ταρτίνι|Giuseppe Tartini|Giuseppe Tartini was an Italian violinist and Baroque composer. He is known for the "Devil's Trill Sonata". He founded a school of violin in Padua.

bio|02-26|1802|Βικτόρ Ουγκώ|Victor Hugo|Victor Hugo was a French writer of the Romantic movement. He wrote "Les Miserables" and "The Hunchback of Notre-Dame". He was also a politician and lived in exile under Napoleon III.

bio|02-26|1821|Ζοσέφ Ντε Μεστρ|Joseph de Maistre|Joseph de Maistre was a French-Savoyard philosopher and diplomat. He was one of the main theorists of the counter-revolution and supported monarchy and the authority of the Church. He died in Turin.

bio|02-26|1928|Αριέλ Σαρόν|Ariel Sharon|Ariel Sharon was born in Palestine under British mandate. He was a general and politician and was prime minister of Israel from 2001 to 2006. In 2005 he ordered the withdrawal from the Gaza Strip.

bio|02-26|1932|Τζόνι Κας|Johnny Cash|Johnny Cash was an American country singer and songwriter. He was known as "The Man in Black". He wrote songs such as "Ring of Fire" and "Folsom Prison Blues" and performed in prisons. He died in 2003.

bio|02-26|1954|Ρετζέπ Ταγίπ Ερντογάν|Recep Tayyip Erdogan|Recep Tayyip Erdogan is a Turkish politician. He was mayor of Istanbul and founded the AK Party. He was prime minister of Turkey from 2003 to 2014, and since 2014 he has been president of the country.

bio|02-26|1959|Αχμέτ Νταβούτογλου|Ahmet Davutoglu|Ahmet Davutoglu is a Turkish politician and academic. He was foreign minister from 2009 to 2014 and prime minister from 2014 to 2016. He is known for his theory of "strategic depth".

bio|02-26|1969|Καρλ Γιάσπερς|Karl Jaspers|Karl Jaspers died in Basel in 1969. He was a German psychiatrist and philosopher, a representative of existentialist philosophy, and he wrote "General Psychopathology" and "The Idea of the University".

bio|02-27|272|Κωνσταντίνος ο Μέγας|Constantine the Great|Constantine the Great was born in Naissus (Nis) and became a Roman emperor. He reunified the empire, and with the Edict of Milan he gave freedom to Christian worship. In 330 he inaugurated Constantinople. He convened the First Ecumenical Council.

bio|02-27|1861|Ρούντολφ Στάινερ|Rudolf Steiner|Rudolf Steiner was an Austrian philosopher and educator. He founded anthroposophy and the Waldorf schools, as well as biodynamic agriculture. He wrote many books and taught in various countries.

bio|02-27|1887|Αλεξάντρ Μποροντίν|Alexander Borodin|Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer and chemist. He was a member of "The Five" and wrote the opera "Prince Igor", with the "Polovtsian Dances". He was also a professor of chemistry.

bio|02-27|1902|Τζον Στάινμπεκ|John Steinbeck|John Steinbeck was an American writer. He wrote the novels "The Grapes of Wrath", "Of Mice and Men" and "East of Eden". In 1962 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-27|1930|Τζοάν Γούντγουορντ|Joanne Woodward|Joanne Woodward was an American actress. She won the Oscar for Best Actress for "The Three Faces of Eve" in 1957. She was married to Paul Newman for fifty years.

bio|02-27|1932|Ελίζαμπεθ Τέιλορ|Elizabeth Taylor|Elizabeth Taylor was a British-American actress. She won Oscars for "Butterfield 8" and "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" and starred in "Cleopatra". She was also an activist against AIDS.

bio|02-27|1936|Ιβάν Πάβλοφ|Ivan Pavlov|Ivan Pavlov was a Russian physiologist. He studied digestion and discovered the conditioned reflex in dogs. In 1904 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|02-27|1989|Κόνραντ Λόρεντς|Konrad Lorenz|Konrad Lorenz was an Austrian zoologist. He founded ethology, the study of animal behaviour, and described the phenomenon of "imprinting" in goslings. In 1973 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|02-27|1993|Λίλιαν Γκις|Lillian Gish|Lillian Gish was an American actress. She was one of the greatest leading actresses of silent film, with films by D. W. Griffith such as "The Birth of a Nation" and "Broken Blossoms". Her career lasted more than eight decades.

bio|02-28|1533|Μισέλ ντε Μονταίν|Michel de Montaigne|Michel de Montaigne was a French writer and philosopher. He wrote the "Essays", in which he reflects on himself and on life, and he created the essay as a literary form. He was also mayor of Bordeaux.

bio|02-28|1869|Αλφόνς ντε Λαμαρτίν|Alphonse de Lamartine|Alphonse de Lamartine was a French poet and politician of the Romantic movement. He wrote the collection "Meditations". He was foreign minister and head of the provisional government after the revolution of 1848.

bio|02-28|1901|Λάινους Πόλινγκ|Linus Pauling|Linus Pauling was an American chemist. He studied the nature of the chemical bond and in 1954 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He was also a pacifist and in 1962 received the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|02-28|1916|Χένρι Τζέιμς|Henry James|Henry James was an American writer who lived in England. He wrote novels such as "The Portrait of a Lady" and "The Turn of the Screw", with subtle psychological analysis. He was the brother of the philosopher William James.

bio|02-28|1930|Λέον Νιλ Κούπερ|Leon N. Cooper|Leon Cooper is an American physicist. Together with Bardeen and Schrieffer he developed the BCS theory of superconductivity, for which they were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1972.

bio|02-28|1942|Ντίνο Τζοφ|Dino Zoff|Dino Zoff was born in Italy and was a goalkeeper. He played for Juventus and the Italian national team and won the 1982 World Cup as captain and goalkeeper, at the age of 40.

bio|02-28|1953|Πωλ Κρούγκμαν|Paul Krugman|Paul Krugman is an American economist and journalist. He studied international trade and economic geography, and in 2008 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. He writes for newspapers on the economy.

bio|02-28|1986|Ούλωφ Πάλμε|Olof Palme|Olof Palme was a Swedish Social Democrat politician and prime minister of Sweden. He was known for his international work in support of peace. He was assassinated in Stockholm in 1986, and the perpetrator is not fully known.

bio|02-28|2026|Αλί Χαμενεΐ|Ali Khamenei|Ali Khamenei was the Supreme Leader of Iran from 1989, when the founder of the Islamic Republic, Khomeini, died. Before becoming Supreme Leader he had served as president of the country in the 1980s.

bio|02-29|1792|Τζοακίνο Ροσίνι|Gioachino Rossini|Gioachino Rossini was an Italian opera composer. He wrote "The Barber of Seville", "Cinderella" and "William Tell". After 1829 he stopped writing operas and wrote mainly smaller works.

bio|02-29|1860|Χέρμαν Χόλεριθ|Herman Hollerith|Herman Hollerith was an American engineer and statistician. He invented the punched-card machine for counting the census of 1890 and founded the company that later became IBM.

bio|02-29|1868|Λουδοβίκος Α΄|Ludwig I|Ludwig I was king of Bavaria from 1825 to 1848. He was a supporter of the arts and a philhellene, and the father of Otto, the first king of Greece. He abdicated after the revolutions of 1848.

bio|02-29|1988|Μπένεντικτ Χέβεντες|Benedikt Howedes|Benedikt Howedes is a German footballer. He played as a defender for Schalke and for the German national team, with which he won the World Cup in 2014.

bio|02-29|2000|Φεράν Τόρες|Ferran Torres|Ferran Torres is a Spanish footballer. He started at Valencia and played for Manchester City and Barcelona. He has had success with the Spanish national team in the European Championship.

bio|03-01|1445|Σάντρο Μποττιτσέλλι|Sandro Botticelli|Sandro Botticelli was an Italian painter of the Renaissance in Florence. He became known for the works "The Birth of Venus" and "Primavera", which depict mythological themes with grace and fine lines.

bio|03-01|1792|Λεοπόλδος Β΄|Leopold II|Leopold II was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire from 1790. Before that he was Grand Duke of Tuscany and carried out reforms. In the few years of his reign he dealt with the French Revolution. He died in 1792.

bio|03-01|1810|Φρεντερίκ Σοπέν|Frederic Chopin|Frederic Chopin was born in Poland and lived in Paris. He was a pianist and composer of the Romantic movement and wrote nocturnes, polonaises, waltzes and scherzos, almost exclusively for piano. He died young, in 1849.

bio|03-01|1911|Ιάκωβος Ερρίκος βαν'τ Χοφ|Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff|Jacobus van 't Hoff was a Dutch chemist. He founded stereochemistry and studied chemical kinetics and osmotic pressure. In 1901 he became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|03-01|1922|Γιτζάκ Ράμπιν|Yitzhak Rabin|Yitzhak Rabin was an Israeli soldier and politician. He was prime minister of Israel, and in 1993 he signed the Oslo Accords with the Palestinians. In 1994 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He was assassinated in 1995.

bio|03-01|1938|Γκαμπριέλε Ντ' Ανούντσιο|Gabriele D'Annunzio|Gabriele D'Annunzio was an Italian poet and soldier. He led the occupation of Fiume in 1919 and influenced Italian fascism. His works have a grand style and love themes.

bio|03-01|1983|Άρθουρ Κέσλερ|Arthur Koestler|Arthur Koestler was born in Budapest and became a writer. He wrote the novel "Darkness at Noon" about the Stalinist purges. He was a former communist and later an anti-communist. He died in 1983.

bio|03-01|1994|Τζάστιν Μπίμπερ|Justin Bieber|Justin Bieber is a Canadian singer. He was discovered on YouTube at a young age and became famous with songs such as "Baby" and "Sorry". He has sold tens of millions of records.

bio|03-02|625|Χασάν ιμπν Αλί|Hasan ibn Ali|Hasan ibn Ali was a grandson of the Prophet Muhammad and the eldest son of Ali and Fatima. He was caliph for a few months in 661 and then gave up his claim in favour of Muawiya. The Shia honour him as the second imam.
